title: Microglia coordinate circadian regulation of glymphatic brain clearance in neuroimmune disease: a conceptual framework
title_zh: 小胶质细胞协调昼夜节律调控脑淋巴系统清除：概念框架
abstract: Abstract The glymphatic system is a brain-wide fluid and solute transport pathway that contributes to cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange and the removal of metabolites, inflammatory mediators, and aggregation-prone proteins. Glymphatic activity is shaped by sleep state, vascular pulsatility, respiration, vasomotion, astrocytic aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization, meningeal lymphatic drainage, and circadian timing. However, key aspects of brain fluid transport remain debated, including the relative roles of perivascular spaces, periarterial basement membrane pathways, intramural periarterial drainage, diffusion, convection, and anesthesia-dependent physiology. These uncertainties are central to neuroimmune disease, where inflammation, sleep disruption, vascular dysfunction, astrocytic disorganization, and microglial state changes frequently coexist. Here, we review evidence that microglia may coordinate circadian regulation of glymphatic brain clearance. Microglia are circadian, purinergic, and morphologically dynamic immune cells positioned near synapses, vessels, astrocytes, and perivascular spaces. Microglial activity appears to be temporally coupled to physiological states and clearance pathways relevant to glymphatic function: microglial surveillance varies across natural sleep-wake states, microglial phagocytosis can compensate for impaired AQP4-dependent clearance, and meningeal lymphatic drainage shapes microglial inflammatory responses. Recent work further shows that microglial morphology, signaling through the P2Y12 receptor (encoded by P2RY12), and glymphatic tracer influx are linked across Zeitgeber time, and that acute P2Y12 blockade can phase-shift glymphatic rhythms and alter sleep architecture. We propose that microglia may act as neuroimmune chronomodulators that influence the timing and spatial organization of clearance rather than as simple enhancers or inhibitors of flow; however, microglial changes may also represent adaptive responses to altered sleep, vascular physiology, astrocytic state, or glymphatic transport. In neuroimmune disease, glymphatic dysfunction may reflect temporal misalignment among microglial state, sleep architecture, vascular dynamics, astrocytic AQP4 polarity, and fluid transport routes. This framework supports temporally resolved experimental designs and translational studies integrating glymphatic imaging, sleep physiology, circadian biomarkers, inflammatory markers, vascular measures, and cognitive outcomes.
abstract_zh: 摘要 脑淋巴系统是一种全脑范围的液体和溶质运输通路，参与脑脊液-间质液交换以及代谢产物、炎症介质和易聚集蛋白的清除。脑淋巴活性受睡眠状态、血管脉动、呼吸、血管运动、星形胶质细胞水通道蛋白-4（AQP4）极化、脑膜淋巴引流和昼夜节律时间的影响。然而，脑液体运输的关键方面仍存在争议，包括周围血管空间、动脉基底膜通路、动脉壁内排泄、扩散、对流以及麻醉相关生理学的相对作用。这些不确定性在神经免疫疾病中尤为重要，因为炎症、睡眠紊乱、血管功能障碍、星形胶质细胞失序和小胶质细胞状态变化经常共存。本文综述了小胶质细胞可能协调脑淋巴系统昼夜节律清除的证据。小胶质细胞具有昼夜节律、嘌呤能和形态动态特征，位于突触、血管、星形胶质细胞和周围血管空间附近。小胶质细胞活性似乎与与脑淋巴功能相关的生理状态和清除通路在时间上耦合：小胶质细胞监视在自然睡眠-觉醒状态间变化，小胶质细胞吞噬可补偿受损的AQP4依赖清除，脑膜淋巴引流塑造小胶质细胞的炎症反应。近期研究进一步显示，小胶质细胞形态、通过P2Y12受体（由P2RY12编码）的信号传导以及脑淋巴示踪物渗入在Zeitgeber时间上相互关联，急性P2Y12阻断可相位移脑淋巴节律并改变睡眠结构。我们提出，小胶质细胞可能充当神经免疫节律调节器，影响清除的时间和空间组织，而非仅仅是流动的增强或抑制因子；然而，小胶质细胞的变化也可能是对睡眠、血管生理、星形胶质细胞状态或脑淋巴运输改变的适应性响应。在神经免疫疾病中，脑淋巴功能障碍可能反映小胶质细胞状态、睡眠结构、血管动力学、星形胶质细胞AQP4极化和液体运输路径之间的时间错位。该框架支持时间分辨实验设计和整合脑淋巴成像、睡眠生理、昼夜节律生物标志物、炎症标志物、血管测量和认知结果的转化研究。
